topic: Renewal follow-up timing map for property managers
hook: If renewal outreach starts at 30 days, the workflow already started late.
captionInstagram:
When should property managers automate renewal follow-up?

Earlier than most teams think. Renewal workflow problems usually start because pricing review, resident signals, owner rules, and staff ownership stay disconnected until the lease is already too close to expiration. By then, the team is reacting instead of operating.

Practical property management automation should start the renewal clock automatically, route the resident into the right lane, surface pricing and approval context, trigger the right follow-up sequence, and write the current status back into the CRM without copy-paste. That is where an AI front desk for property managers becomes useful across SMS, AI voice, CRM workflows, and front-desk follow-up.

If your renewals still depend on spreadsheets, calendar reminders, or whoever remembered to check the lease report, the issue is not effort. The workflow timing is weak.

slides.title: If renewal outreach starts at 30 days,
slides.body: Pricing review, resident intent, owner rules, and follow-up ownership should be moving before the lease enters the panic window.
slides.footer: Swipe for the 6 timing rules that protect renewals

slides.title: Every lease needs an automatic renewal clock.
slides.body: The workflow should open from the lease-end date and create the first review window automatically instead of waiting for someone to pull a report.
slides.footer: Goal: no lease enters renewal season unseen

slides.title: Not every resident should get the same renewal path.
slides.body: Likely renewals, high-risk churn, delinquency cases, heavy service history, and owner-sensitive units should split into separate lanes before outreach starts.
slides.footer: Goal: one timing map, multiple operating lanes

slides.title: Pricing and approval context should exist before the first message goes out.
slides.body: Market rent, owner rules, concession limits, notice timing, and unit strategy should be attached early so staff are not promising terms they cannot support.
slides.footer: Goal: outreach with policy context already attached

slides.title: Renewal follow-up should escalate by resident behavior, not by staff memory.
slides.body: Viewed but no reply, verbal interest, requested change, or no response should each trigger a different SMS, call, task, or manager-review sequence.
slides.footer: Goal: clean next step for every resident state

slides.title: Special cases need a named owner before the thread gets messy.
slides.body: Transfer requests, hardship cases, roommate changes, month-to-month requests, or policy exceptions should route to a human lane with summary and deadline attached.
slides.footer: Goal: edge cases escalate before follow-up stalls

slides.title: Renewal status belongs in the system your team already works from.
slides.body: Clock start, current lane, latest resident signal, proposed terms, owner, and next deadline should write back so the team does not rebuild renewal status from inbox threads.
slides.footer: Goal: one record shows timing, owner, and next move
